comparison: Both evaluate the core familiarity-based feeding plasticity claims (C1, C8-C13). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate controls and statistical significance. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to major concerns about day-to-day variability in feeding rates (100 pumps/min) being larger than the familiarity effect (20 pumps/min), questioning whether experimental design adequately controls for this variability and whether all experiments were done on the same day. Peer reviewers also note lack of all pairwise bacterial comparisons limits generalizability.

Both evaluate serotonin signaling claims (C14-C17). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with converging genetic and pharmacological evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing concern that 'control pumping rates on the very low side' in Figures 4b, 5a make it unclear whether pumping rates could go lower, questioning whether negative conclusions (tph-1 mutant showing no familiarity discrimination) are warranted.

OpenEval evaluates SER-7 receptor claims (C18-C21, C29-C30) as SUPPORTED, noting sound methodology but complex statistics. Peer review R3 evaluates broader receptor and epistasis claims (C18-C31) as UNCERTAIN, applying general concerns about day-to-day variability and low baseline pumping rates. Peer reviewers specifically mention Figure 8c-d concerns about drawing negative conclusions from low control values, and note lack of complete pairwise bacterial comparisons.

OpenEval evaluates opposing serotonin signals and epistasis (C22-C28) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R3 includes these claims in their UNCERTAIN evaluation alongside receptor claims, citing concerns about variability and low baseline rates affecting interpretation of genetic epistasis experiments. Both note the lack of mechanistic explanation for bacterial strain-specific differences.

Both evaluate ADF neuron identification claims (C37-C39, C45-C47). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with robust convergence of rescue, ablation, and MOD-5 independence data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, specifically citing Figure 8c-d (ADF ablation) as having 'control pumping rates on the very low side' that raise concerns about negative conclusions. They also request direct functional evidence by asking 'Is it possible to elicit pharyngeal pumping by ADF activation?'

Both evaluate MC neuron as SER-7 target (C52-C54, C57-C58). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong cell-specific rescue and eat-2 epistasis evidence. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, appearing to accept this as one of the few results not directly affected by their variability concerns. Both note the eat-2 epistasis demonstrates MC acts through cholinergic transmission.

Both evaluate ADF calcium imaging claims (C60-C63). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes sample sizes not clearly stated and slow activation time course (~120s) is notable. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing concern that 'the lack of a second comparison is more problematic in the Ca++ imaging study' (not all pairwise bacterial combinations tested) and requesting detailed methodological information about R values, exponential fits, bleaching rates, and individual channel values.

Both evaluate serotonin release assay claims (C64-C66). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to indirect assay method, complex statistical analysis (Fisher's method), and inability to definitively distinguish increased release from increased uptake efficiency. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED without raising specific concerns about the immunohistochemistry data showing increased serotonin-positive cells on familiar food.

Both evaluate conditioned media experiments (C67-C70). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate experimental design showing asymmetric effect (novel media suppress familiar food response but not vice versa). Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED without raising specific concerns, appearing to accept this mechanistic insight into how novel bacteria override familiar food responses.

Both evaluate MOD-5 serotonin transporter claims (C40-C41, C43-C44). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting immunohistochemistry clearly shows serotonin in non-ADF neurons with functional MOD-5, though C41 is speculative about mechanisms. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED without specific critique, accepting the conclusion that ADF acts humorally based on mod-5 independence data.

Both evaluate male worm experiments ruling out HSN involvement (C34). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as straightforward control with sound logic. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED without raising concerns about this negative result.

OpenEval evaluates nutritional quality control claim (C7) as SUPPORTED based on appropriate citation to Avery and Shtonda, 2003. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background/control claim.

OpenEval evaluates multiple background/literature claims (C32-C33, C35-C36, C42, C48-C51, C55-C56) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations to established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates background claims on familiarity discrimination across species and C. elegans capabilities (C71-C78) as SUPPORTED, though noting C74-C75 include speculative evolutionary explanations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory/contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates discussion/speculative claims (C79-C91) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are primarily speculative interpretations about evolutionary advantage, natural behavior, or mechanistic explanations, with C84 citing unpublished data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these discussion points.
